Dota 2's Behavior and Communication System Needs a Serious Rework

Dota sell u voicelines u use voicelines after u manage to escape or kill someone on funny way and u get instant reported for toxic. I had so many games where i see that msg player is banned from using chat till end of match right after he use the voiceline and it has happend to me too.

Valve sells these voice lines, but players can end up afraid to use them because they might get reported. I'm not saying every case proves the system is wrong, but these situations are evidence that the system deserves scrutiny. Having 12k behaviour score doesn't prove it never makes mistakes, either.

Dota 2's Behavior and Communication System Needs a Serious Rework
18 Oct @ 9:45am
Hiroshi
Experienced players rely on contextual, real-time judgment, whereas automated systems rely on strict, non-contextual metrics. Until report and Overwatch systems place greater weight on contextual behavioral anomalies.

High-hour players will continue to catch these issues , what makes it worse is bringing this up on the forums, only to get low-level accounts (level 0 to private accounts) giving automated, out-of-context replies ("the system works fine for me").

On top of that, undeserved mass-reports from these exact bots/griefers tank behavior scores for real players.

Unfair Punishment System Is Ruining Dota 2
18 Oct @ 3:41am
⫘Mr. Boombastic⫘
[/quote]

He wouldn't dare provide evidence for further action. In Dota 2, evaluations are handled by a system—a system that, unlike a human, does not let emotions influence its decision-making. If you accuse someone (via the player reporting system) and the system finds no evidence to support it, your action is categorized as harassment.
In short, these assessments are carried out by a system designed to ensure that the game remains an enjoyable experience for everyone.
